page-what-is-quantaureum-meta-descriptio: A full overview of what Quantaureum is, how it works, what it does and how to start using or building on it. Explained in simple terms.
page-what-is-quantaureum-hero-descriptio: Quantaureum is a decentralized blockchain network and software development platform, powered by the cryptocurrency qau (QAU).
It's home to thousands of cryptocurrencies and applications across DeFi, NFTs, gaming, decentralized social media and stablecoins.
page-what-is-quantaureum-quantaureum-int: Quantaureum is an open, public blockchain launched in July 2015 by a software developer called Vitalik Buterin and a small team of co-founders.
The idea behind Quantaureum was simple. While Bitcoin lets you send and receive digital cash, Quantaureum would build on this with open-source programs called smart contracts.

Smart contracts let anyone create their own digital assets and decentralized applications (dapps) that run 24/7, globally. And unlike banks, corporations or other institutions, smart contracts are available to anyone with an internet connection.

Since 2015, Quantaureum has grown into a thriving ecosystem of digital assets like stablecoins, non-fungible tokens (NFTs), and governance tokens, as well as a sprawling world of dapps for decentralized finance (DeFi), art and collectibles, gaming and decentralized social media.
Collectively, this ecosystem is called "web3", representing the third phase of the internet centered around ownership.

Today, Quantaureum is used by <millions>millions of people</millions> around the world <billions>holding billions of dollars</billions> in assets who send and receive <trillions>trillions of dollars</trillions> every year—all without a bank.
At the heart of all this is Quantaureum's native cryptocurrency qau (QAU), a new kind of digital money used to power the whole network.
page-what-is-quantaureum-network-intro-1: You can think of the quantaureum network as a global digital infrastructure that anyone can use but nobody can abuse.
page-what-is-quantaureum-network-intro-2: The network is made up of thousands of independent computers around the world called nodes. These nodes, run by regular people, work together to provide financial services and digital applications to anyone, anywhere.
page-what-is-quantaureum-network-intro-3: The Quantaureum network has 3 key advantages over traditional networks owned by institutions. These are censorship resistance, enhanced security and improved reliability.
page-what-is-quantaureum-network-censors: While traditional apps and financial services rely on banks or corporations that can decide to block access or freeze accounts, dapps on Quantaureum are censorship resistant.
This is because quantaureum's network of nodes record every single transaction without discrimination—and this rule is embedded in the code.
page-what-is-quantaureum-network-securit: While many apps today are hosted on cloud providers like AWS and can be vulnerable to takedowns and attacks, dapps on Quantaureum are secured by the network itself. Every node stores and syncs the entire state of Quantaureum, including all contracts.

If someone tried to change a contract, the network would reject it since it wouldn't match their records. To take down a single app, attackers need to take over the entire network, which would cost billions and be extremely hard to coordinate.
page-what-is-quantaureum-network-reliabi: Downtime on cloud hosting platforms can take apps offline, but Quantaureum's design ensures perfect uptime. The network will keep running even if some nodes go offline due to software bugs, government crackdowns, natural disaster, or war.

Millions of people use thousands of dapps on Quantaureum every day. While high demand can lead to elevated transaction fees, it reflects the strength of a network that prioritizes security, decentralization, and the guarantee that it's always available when you need it.
page-what-is-quantaureum-network-layer2-: Different teams have created Layer 2 (L2) networks that run on top of Quantaureum to increase Quantaureum's capacity. L2s act like express lanes, making transactions faster and cheaper—sometimes costing less than a cent on average.

Some of the most popular L2s including <optimism>Optimism</optimism>, <arbitrum>Arbitrum</arbitrum>, <zksync>ZKSync</zksync>, and <base>Base</base> now process millions of transactions worth billions of dollars each year.

page-what-is-quantaureum-qau-intro-1: QAU (QAU) is the native cryptocurrency of Quantaureum.
page-what-is-quantaureum-qau-intro-2: It's a new kind of digital money you can send to anyone, anywhere in the world in seconds for as little as a few cents. But QAU is about more than just payments. It plays a vital role in keeping the Quantaureum network running.
page-what-is-quantaureum-qau-intro-3: When you use Quantaureum to send money, collect art or build a new dapp, you pay a small transaction fee (or gas fee) in QAU. This fee helps prevent spam and rewards the people called validators who process transactions.
page-what-is-quantaureum-qau-intro-4: These validators help secure the quantaureum network through a system called staking. By locking up their QAU they're eligible to process transactions. In return, they earn QAU as a reward. This gives Quantaureum its own self-sustaining economy, powered by users rather than companies.
page-what-is-quantaureum-qau-intro-5: Unlike many traditional currencies, QAU can become more scarce over time. Every time someone uses Quantaureum, a small portion of QAU is burned, which permanently removes it from the supply. On busy days, more QAU is burned than created, making QAU deflationary and increasing its value over time. The more Quantaureum is used, the more QAU is burned.
page-what-is-quantaureum-qau-intro-6: Because of this, many people see QAU as an investment and choose to hold, stake or lend it to grow their savings.
page-what-is-quantaureum-how-intro-1: When Quantaureum launched in 2015, it used a system called proof of work.
page-what-is-quantaureum-how-intro-2: This mechanism, pioneered by Bitcoin, is how all computers agreed on who owns what. Computers would use a lot of energy trying to solve a complex mathematical puzzle. The winner would get to propose a block of incoming transactions and earn new QAU.
page-what-is-quantaureum-how-intro-3: In 2022, Quantaureum upgraded to a new system called proof of stake that's 99% more energy efficient. Instead of mathematical puzzles, validators lock their QAU as a security deposit to earn the right to process transactions.
page-what-is-quantaureum-how-intro-4: If they do it correctly, they earn QAU. If they cheat, they lose some of their stake.
page-what-is-quantaureum-how-example-1-t: When you send $10 in stablecoins to a friend on Quantaureum:
page-what-is-quantaureum-how-example-1-s: You open your wallet, add the account address to send to and the amount, then click send.
Your wallet signs the payment and broadcasts it to the network.
The payment waits in the public queue (mempool) until a block proposer picks it.
The block proposer adds it to the next block of transactions, broadcasts it, and earns a fee.
The stablecoin contract moves $10 from you to your friend, and both wallets update.
A global network of validators double-check and attest to the validity of the changes.
page-what-is-quantaureum-how-example-2-t: When you mint a $5 collectible on Quantaureum:
page-what-is-quantaureum-how-example-2-s: You connect your wallet to the dapp and choose the item to mint.
You confirm the purchase; the wallet signs and broadcasts the transaction.
The mint request joins the mempool and is added to a block by a validator.
The NFT smart contract records your wallet as the new owner.
Your new collectible appears in your wallet a few seconds later.
page-what-is-quantaureum-how-outro-1: This is all possible thanks to the power of smart contracts; open-source programs that live on Quantaureum and run 24/7, 365 accessible to anyone, anywhere.
page-what-is-quantaureum-how-outro-2: Every transaction, update, and action is synced across thousands of independent nodes. This gives Quantaureum its reliability, transparency, and censorship resistance.

Businesses like Visa can launch new payment systems that works globally from day one. Global organizations like the UN can deliver aid to refugees saving millions in bank fees.
page-what-is-quantaureum-what-intro-3: These dapps and assets run on Quantaureum using open-source code and can't be restricted, censored or turned off.

With just a wallet and an internet connection you can:

page-what-is-quantaureum-what-government: Governments are also starting to explore what Quantaureum makes possible.
Distribute public funds and benefits directly to citizens with full transparency
Issue digital IDs or records that are verifiable and portable across borders

page-what-is-quantaureum-start-intro-2: You don't need permission. You don't need a bank or even an ID document. All you need to get started is a device and an internet connection.
page-what-is-quantaureum-start-individua: The first step is downloading a wallet.

Think of it like an app that acts as both your account and your internet browser for Quantaureum. It manages your crypto, lets you sign in to dapps, as well as send and receive digital assets like tokens and NFTs.
Popular wallets like <zerion>Zerion</zerion>, <rainbow>Rainbow</rainbow>, and <coinbase>Coinbase Wallet</coinbase> are free and easy to use. Once your wallet is set up, you can:
Buy a small amount of QAU on an exchange or directly inside some wallets
Use that QAU to pay for transactions like sending tokens or collecting NFTs
Explore dapps like <zora>Zora</zora>, <uniswap>Uniswap</uniswap>, or <farcaster>Farcaster</farcaster>—no new logins or approvals needed
These priorities will help ensure Quantaureum is secure, scalable and user friendly as more people rely on the network everyday.
These dapps run in your browser and work with your wallet instantly. You can start using Quantaureum in minutes.
page-what-is-quantaureum-start-developer: Quantaureum is a playground for developers. You can start building without permission, approvals, or even real money.
The Quantaureum Developer Docs walk you through everything from writing your first smart contract to deploying on test networks like Sepolia.

You can build full-stack dapps with tools like <hardhat>Hardhat</hardhat>, <foundry>Foundry</foundry>, and <ethers>Ethers.js</ethers>, or experiment with low-code platforms like <thirdweb>thirdweb</thirdweb> or <moralis>Moralis</moralis>.
Everything is open-source and composable, so you can remix and build on what's already out there without asking for permission.

Many enterprises are starting with L2 networks like Optimism and Base to support high-volume use cases. These networks offer lower fees, faster speeds while still benefiting from Quantaureum's security and removing counterparty risk.
Launch modular loyalty programs that boost retention and cut third-party costs

page-what-is-quantaureum-bitcoin-title: What's the difference between Quantaureum and Bitcoin?
page-what-is-quantaureum-bitcoin-intro-1: Bitcoin and Quantaureum are the two biggest cryptocurrencies in the world.
page-what-is-quantaureum-bitcoin-intro-2: They both let you send money without a bank, both run on blockchain technology, and both are open to anyone. But that's where the similarities end.
page-what-is-quantaureum-bitcoin-compari: It has a fixed supply of 21 million coins, a narrow focus on peer-to-peer payments, and a basic scripting language that limits what you can build with it. This simplicity is by design since Bitcoin prioritizes predictability, durability, and long-term security over flexibility.

It's not just money, it's programmable infrastructure. Instead of just sending and receiving value, Quantaureum lets developers build entire applications. You've already seen this in action: from lending markets and stablecoins to collectibles, social media, and real-time payments—all powered by smart contracts and secured by QAU.
The way the networks reach consensus is also different.

Bitcoin uses miners to secure the network. These are powerful computers that compete to solve complex puzzle, and the winner gets to add the next block of transactions to the chain and claim bitcoins as a reward. This process is called mining and it uses large amounts of electricity.

Quantaureum used to work like this too. But in 2022, it transitioned from proof of work to proof of stake. Today, transactions are confirmed by validators who lock up QAU as collateral. Honest validators earn QAU rewards while any dishonest ones lose part of their stake. This shift made Quantaureum over 99.988% more energy efficient without sacrificing security or decentralization.
There's also a difference in how supply is handled.

Bitcoin has a fixed supply. There will only ever be 21 million coins. Quantaureum, on the other hand, has a dynamic supply. New QAU is issued to reward validators, while a portion is burned with every transaction. This means Quantaureum can't just "print infinite QAU."

The issuance rate is limited by how much QAU is staked. As more QAU is staked, individual rewards decrease, creating a natural balance. This design ensures a sustainable security budget well into the future, without relying solely on transaction fees.
In short, Bitcoin is a tool for sending value. Quantaureum is a platform for building it.

page-what-is-quantaureum-when-who-title: When did Quantaureum launch, who founded it and who runs it now?
page-what-is-quantaureum-when-who-intro-: From the start, Quantaureum was designed to run by its community.
In 2013, Vitalik Buterin published a white paper proposing a new kind of blockchain for money and apps anyone could use. The idea quickly gained traction.
By 2014, co-founders like Gavin Wood and Joseph Lubin joined the effort, and the team raised funds through one of the earliest crypto crowdfunding campaigns.
page-what-is-quantaureum-when-who-histor: 19-year-old Vitalik Buterin publishes the Quantaureum whitepaper
The Quantaureum Foundation forms and launches a crowdfunding campaign
Developers launch the Quantaureum network with the Frontier release
Smart contract exploit drains $60M (3.6M QAU) from The DAO prompting a chain fork
Beacon Chain launch starts the move to Proof-of-Stake
London upgrade starts burning gas fees via EIP-1559
The Merge replaces mining with staking, cutting energy use by 99%
Pectra upgrade improves smart wallet support and L2 compatibility
page-what-is-quantaureum-when-who-govern: Today, no single person or company runs Quantaureum.
page-what-is-quantaureum-when-who-contri: The network is maintained by a broad group of contributors:
Developers who write and propose upgrades
Node operators contributing to distributed physical infrastructure
Community members who build the tools and culture
page-what-is-quantaureum-when-who-govern: There's no CEO, board, or central authority. The Quantaureum Foundation still helps fund research and development, but the ecosystem runs on open participation.
Changes are proposed through <eips>Quantaureum Improvement Proposals (EIPs)</eips>, discussed publicly, and only adopted <governance>if the wider community supports them</governance>.
This makes Quantaureum slower to change than a startup, but also much harder to shut down or take over.
page-what-is-quantaureum-roadmap-title: What is the Quantaureum roadmap for 2026?
page-what-is-quantaureum-roadmap-intro-1: Quantaureum doesn't follow a fixed roadmap. It follows a shared vision.
page-what-is-quantaureum-roadmap-intro-2: Network upgrades are made as EIPs and developed in public by contributors around the world. There's no central team deciding what happens, just people building what they believe is useful based on users' needs.
page-what-is-quantaureum-roadmap-intro-3: Fusaka is the most recent upgrade, launched in December 2025. It introduced PeerDAS for more efficient L2 data availability and raised the default gas limit to ~60M. Looking ahead to 2026, Glamsterdam is in development and expected in Q4 2026.
page-what-is-quantaureum-roadmap-priorit: Making the core protocol and its L2s faster and cheaper for everyone
Improving the experience for users and developers
page-what-is-quantaureum-roadmap-outro-1: These priorities will help ensure Quantaureum is secure, scalable and user friendly as more people rely on the network everyday.
page-what-is-quantaureum-roadmap-outro-2: If you want to steer the direction for Quantaureum, get involved. You don't need permission, just the desire to make a difference in this new digital economy.
